packing_court.name: Packing Court
packing_court.description: Two benches facing each other across one floor, both driven by one word. `packing` is a two-member family - example_8_3_recursion_circles_vr and sierpinski_pyramid, both declaring fused | contact | open | dust character for character - and the hypothesis that they are about the same thing is FALSE, provably from the line each one consumes the value on. The circles read it inside the recursion (gd:195, `new_radius := radius * radius_reduction`), so it is the similitude ratio and every value is a different attractor: the similarity dimension runs 2.714 | 2.000 | 1.321 | 1.000 across the four rungs. The pyramid reads it once, after the recursion has finished, in _spawn_cube (gd:206-207), so the lattice, the census and the dimension are identical in all four and only the ink changes. Same word, one generative parameter and one rendering parameter. The left bench runs the ratio mechanism and the right bench the fill mechanism, side by side, at the same rung, in every frame. The second axis asks which part of the packing is made of matter - the atoms, the clear space between them drawn as solids, or the incidences at a fixed gauge - and it is the reading that catches them: under `web` the fill bench's 125 dots do not move at any value of the axis and the ratio bench's 21 move at all of them. The one rung where the two agree is `contact`, and they agree exactly: 2*offset = 2*r solves to r = 0.5 and fill = 1.0 is one lattice pitch, so both clear gaps are 0.000 m, and reading=gap therefore draws NOTHING at contact and nothing at fused - the designed null, and the finding, are the same two frames. No RandomNumberGenerator, no randf, no noise, no _process, no Timer.
dev_themes: a word held at two depths of one construction
a lattice that does not listen
interactions: stand at reading=web and walk the packing axis. The right bench does not move. Not subtly - not at all: its 125 dots are at the same coordinates at fused, contact, open and dust, because sierpinski_pyramid's PACKING_FILL is consumed in _spawn_cube after the recursion has placed every leaf. The left bench's 21 dots move at every rung. That is the whole finding in one sweep of one axis

set reading=gap and compare fused against contact. Both are an empty court, and it is the only exact agreement the two members have: the ratio bench's clear span is 2R(1 - 2r) and the fill bench's is (1 - fill)*LEAF, and those two expressions cross zero at the same rung of the same word

compare gap at open against gap at dust. The gap gets LONGER and THINNER, and the total falls - 0.144 of a leaf volume per pair at open against 0.056 at dust. A gap is a relation between two atoms, not what is left over when they shrink, and at dust the atoms are too small to bound much of anything

count the rings at every value of packing on the left bench: 21, always. Count the cubes on the right: 125, always. Neither bench changes its census - the extent of the ratio bench does not move either, because every child is exactly internally tangent to its parent at any ratio. Everything that is conserved is conserved in both, which is exactly why the word looked like one word

look at kept=dust on the left bench. Each of the three generations contributes the same total centreline, 0.44 m of it, because 4r = 1 at r = 0.25 - the ratio bench's dimension is exactly 1 there. Now look at the right bench in the same frame: its dimension has not moved from log(5)/log(2) = 2.322 and cannot, at any value of this axis
packing_court.capacity: SEE that two artifacts can declare one axis, one value list and one order, and still be asking different questions - and learn to find out which by asking WHERE IN THE CONSTRUCTION the value is consumed, rather than what the registry says it means

spatial_needs.footprint_note: THE FLOOR IS THE FOOTPRINT AND IT IS DRAWN BEFORE EITHER AXIS IS CONSULTED: a 2.40 x 0.05 x 1.15 slab, two 1.10 x 0.012 x 1.02 pads at x = -0.60 and +0.60, and a 0.026 x 0.014 x 1.02 divider strip on the centre line. Four meshes, identical in all twelve cells. They are the reason the AABB is a constant and the reason the two designed-null frames are a picture of an empty court rather than a blank plate. Everything the axes draw is furniture-free above them: the pads are 12 mm proud and the divider 14 mm, so nothing in the court can stand in front of a mark. The content clears the floor edge at every value - the fill bench is widest at fused, spanning x from 0.078 to 1.122 against a floor half-width of 1.200, and z to +-0.522 against a half-depth of 0.575.

dna.default: packing=contact, reading=kept. THE DEFAULT IS THE ONE RUNG THE TWO MEMBERS AGREE ON, and it is also a split decision made honestly: sierpinski_pyramid ships `contact` (gd:65) and example_8_3 ships `fused` (gd:65). Two members, two defaults, no majority - and the tie is broken on the only value in the list that is DERIVED rather than chosen in both mechanisms at once. On the ratio bench 2*offset = 2*r solves to r = 0.5 exactly, the unique ratio at which two in-plane siblings are tangent, at which the drawn measure is conserved (4r^2 = 1) and at which the similarity dimension is exactly 2. On the fill bench fill = 1.0 is exactly one lattice pitch, so leaves meet face to face and nothing overlaps. Both clear gaps are 0.000 m at that rung and at no other. reading=kept because it is the only reading either source has: both draw their survivors and nothing else, so the default cell is the two members' own pictures standing next to each other, unedited.
dna.note:
THE FAMILY IS TWO MEMBERS, SO THERE IS EXACTLY ONE COMPARISON AND NOTHING TO TRIANGULATE AGAINST. The census first:

  example_8_3_recursion_circles_vr  packing = fused | contact | open | dust   default fused
  sierpinski_pyramid                packing = fused | contact | open | dust   default contact

Identical words, identical order, and each member's registry says the other's name. THE HYPOTHESIS THAT THEY ARE ABOUT THE SAME THING IS FALSE, and the disproof is one line in each file - not what the value MEANS, but WHERE IT IS CONSUMED.

  RATIO   example_8_3 gd:70 maps the four words onto {0.6, 0.5, 0.35, 0.25} and hands them to
          `radius_reduction`, which _draw_circles reads INSIDE the recursion, at gd:195 for
          the child radius and gd:196 for the offset. Every value is therefore a different
          attractor. With a 4-fold branch at ratio r the similarity dimension is
          log(4)/log(1/r): fused 2.7138, contact 2.0000, open 1.3205, dust 1.0000. The axis
          walks a fractal from dimension 2.71 - above the plane it is drawn in, so the open
          set condition fails and the figure self-overlaps - down through exactly 2 to
          exactly 1. THE TWO ENDS OF THIS AXIS ARE NOT THE SAME OBJECT AT DIFFERENT SIZES.

  FILL    sierpinski_pyramid gd:52 maps the same four words onto {1.35, 1.0, 0.6, 0.28} and
          the table is read in ONE place, _spawn_cube gd:206-207, after the recursion has
          finished placing every leaf. `packing` cannot reach _recursive_build. The lattice,
          the census and the Hausdorff dimension are identical in all four values; only the
          leaf's edge changes. It is a dilation of a fixed point set, and the file says so
          in its own header - `the measure argument, not a size knob`. That description is
          exactly right about ITS member and exactly wrong about the other one.

SO THE WORD NAMES A GENERATIVE PARAMETER IN ONE MEMBER AND A RENDERING PARAMETER IN THE OTHER. That is a real difference and it hides well, because everything a reader would check agrees: both keep their census fixed (21 rings and 125 cubes here, at every value), both keep their extent fixed to first order, both run more-to-less in the same direction, and both put `contact` at the tangency rung. The court is built so the two mechanisms stand at the same rung in the same photograph and can be caught.

THE ONE RUNG WHERE THEY AGREE, AND IT IS EXACT. The ratio bench's clear span between opposed siblings is 2R(1 - 2r); the fill bench's clear span between face-adjacent leaves is (1 - fill)*LEAF. Both cross zero at `contact` - r = 0.5 and fill = 1.0 - and both are negative at `fused`. That coincidence is not decoration; it is why the vocabulary looked like one vocabulary, and it is this artifact's designed null.

THREE THINGS THIS COURT REPAIRS, all checkable from the lines named, and all found by reading rather than by capturing.

  1. SIERPINSKI_PYRAMID MAKES SIX CHILDREN PER LEVEL, NOT FIVE. _recursive_build calls itself
     at gd:109 (top at +half_size) and AGAIN at gd:174 (top at +offset), plus four bottoms at
     gd:177-180. Its @identity says `pyramid(depth) = 5 * pyramid(depth-1)`; its registry
     says 625 cubes at the shipped depth and 3125 at `limit`. The code makes 6^4 = 1296 calls
     at 1236 distinct positions, and 6^5 = 7776 at limit - two and a half times the number
     the still_note's watchdog warning was sized against. THE PROOF WAS ALREADY IN THE
     REGISTRY AND NOBODY READ IT: measurements.aabb_size is [8.5, 12.25, 8.5], measured
     2026-04-29. A five-child pyramid on that lattice measures 8.5 cubed. The doubled top is
     the 12.25, and it has sat there contradicting the formula for four months.
  2. ITS `contact` IS NOT CONTACT. The header at gd:28-30 says the leaves sit `on a lattice
     whose spacing is exactly size` so that at fill = 1.0 `the atoms touch`. The initial
     extent at gd:96 is size * pow(2, depth - 1), which makes the finest offset size/4 and
     the leaf pitch size/4; a cube of edge `size` therefore overlaps its nearest neighbour
     four to one, and even the five-child version would overlap two to one. The file's own
     comment at gd:198 names the fix - `Initial call size: size * pow(2, depth)` - inside a
     block of thinking-aloud that was never applied. So the shipped picture is already fused,
     and `fused` at 1.35 is a marginal increase on a solid. This court uses LEAF * 2^depth;
     the minimum Chebyshev separation between its 125 leaves is then exactly LEAF, measured,
     so contact is exact face tangency.
  3. EXAMPLE_8_3 NEVER ROTATES ITS TORI. _create_circle gd:203-214 sets a position and no
     rotation, and Godot's TorusMesh is generated around its local +Y, lying in XZ - the
     convention seven other artifacts in this repo write into their own comments. The offsets
     at gd:198-201 are in XY. So a planar circle-packing figure is drawn with every ring
     standing perpendicular to the plane the packing happens in, and the internal tangency
     its registry celebrates at length is arithmetic the picture cannot show. Here the rings
     are rotated into the plane of their own offsets.

WHAT THE VALUES DRAW, BENCH BY BENCH.

  fused    r 0.60 / fill 1.35. Past the closing point in both. In-plane siblings overlap by
           0.2 of the parent radius and the ring field reads as interference; each leaf
           overflows its cell by 0.175 of an edge and the finest holes close into carved
           rock. example_8_3's shipped value.
  contact  r 0.50 / fill 1.00. Tangency in both, derived in both, and the only rung at which
           the two mechanisms make the same claim. sierpinski_pyramid's shipped value.
  open     r 0.35 / fill 0.60. Daylight in both. The ratio bench stops being a texture and
           reads as a branching tree; the fill mountain opens.
  dust     r 0.25 / fill 0.28. Small and far in both, AND THE ASYMMETRY IS AT ITS WIDEST
           HERE: on the ratio bench 4r = 1, so every generation contributes exactly the same
           total centreline (0.44 m of it) and the dimension is exactly 1 - the figure has
           become a curve. On the fill bench 97.8 percent of the drawn volume is gone
           (0.28^3 = 0.0220) and the dimension has not moved at all.

THE SECOND AXIS IS A READING, NOT A STYLE, and the three sets it draws are disjoint. `kept` is
the survivors, which is the only reading either source has. `gap` is the clear space between
neighbours drawn as solid - a cross of two bars per parent on the ratio bench, spanning
2R(1 - 2r), and the exact complement prism between each face-adjacent leaf pair on the fill
bench, (1-fill)*LEAF long and (fill*LEAF) square. `web` is the incidences at a fixed gauge
that ignores how big anything is: a dot at every atom centre, a rod wherever two atoms touch
or overlap. IT IS THE READING THAT CATCHES THEM, because it isolates position: the fill
bench's 125 dots are at identical coordinates at all four values and the ratio bench's 21 are
not at any two.

TWO SMALLER THINGS THE `web` READING MADE VISIBLE, both measured on the geometry. Parent-to-
child is an incidence at EVERY ratio and never breaks, because offset + rR = R(1-r) + rR = R
identically - containment survives the whole axis and only neighbourhood does not. And the
fill bench has the SAME 406 incidences at fused and at contact, because no leaf pair sits at
a Chebyshev distance between 1.00 and 1.35 lattice pitches: the contact graph of a lattice
cannot tell those two values apart. Neither of those is registrable as a null - each is half
a frame - but both are the same sentence as the exhibit.

predicted_degeneracy.pair: open against dust, in the web reading
predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic:
THE CONTEXT IS THE `web` COLUMN and the ranking is computed inside it. Camera is capture_config_sweep's - FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760 - with dna.framing 0.56 on a union AABB of 2.4000 x 1.1519 x 1.1500, diagonal 2.899882, so the frame is 2.899882 x 1.9 x 0.56 = 3.085475 m across in every cell, 4.0598 mm per pixel, frame area 9.5202 m2.

WHY THIS PAIR IS THE FLOOR, AND IT IS BY CONSTRUCTION ON BOTH HALVES. The RIGHT bench is byte-identical in the two frames: its 125 dots sit at the leaf lattice, which sierpinski_pyramid's packing cannot reach, and it draws ZERO rods in both, because the lattice minimum separation is exactly LEAF while the reach is 0.6*LEAF and 0.28*LEAF. Half the court is the same photograph twice. The LEFT bench has the same census in both - 21 dots and 20 parent-to-child rods, and no sibling rods at either value, since siblings clear each other only at r >= 0.5 - so nothing appears or disappears and only POSITION moves.

THE NUMBER. Level-1 dots stand at R0(1-r): 0.44 x 0.65 = 0.28600 at open against 0.44 x 0.75 = 0.33000 at dust, 0.04400 m apart. Level-2 dots stand at R0(1-r) +- R0*r(1-r): open 0.28600 +- 0.10010 = 0.18590 and 0.38610, dust 0.33000 +- 0.08250 = 0.24750 and 0.41250, so those shift 0.06160 and 0.02640. A dot is 0.048 m across, so the shifts are 0.55 to 1.28 diameters and most but not all of each dot clears its old place. Ink: 21 dots at pi x 0.024^2 = 0.038000 m2; rods 4 x 0.28600 + 16 x 0.10010 = 2.74560 m of centreline at open and 4 x 0.33000 + 16 x 0.08250 = 2.64000 m at dust, times a 0.016 m gauge = 0.043930 and 0.042240 m2. Total moving ink 0.081930 m2 at open. A flat-shaded painter's-order replica at the standpoint above, scored by cabinet_sweep's own test (subject if sum-abs RGB from the backdrop > 26, changed if sum-abs RGB between frames > 26, over the whole 577600 px frame), gives 0.05798 m2 = 0.609 percent - 71 percent of the moving ink clearing itself. REGISTERED AT 0.61.

THE CROSS-CHECK THAT MAKES IT WORTH MAKING. `fused against contact, in the web reading` is the same structural situation - the right bench is byte-identical there too, and for a second reason: no leaf pair sits at a Chebyshev distance between 1.00 and 1.35 lattice pitches, so the contact graph is the SAME 406 rods at both values. The only difference is that the left bench there also carries 30 sibling rods, which move. The replica measures 1.068 percent, a ratio of 1.75 to the named pair, and that ratio is what the sibling rods are worth. So the prediction is really two numbers and an ORDER: 0.61 then 1.07. If the sweep returns them in the other order, the fill bench is moving when the source says it cannot, and every number in the sheet is a fact about a broken lattice rather than about the axis.

THE REST OF THE COLUMN, for the ranking: web fused-open 3.379, web contact-dust 3.419, web contact-open 3.435, web fused-dust 3.464. The named pair is smaller than the next non-null by 1.75x and than the rest of its column by 5.5x.

THE PREDICTION IS A FLOOR, NOT A FORECAST. The replica has one key, flat shading, no shadows, no ambient occlusion, no antialiasing and no specular; every prior prediction in this corpus has under-read by 1.5x to 6.7x. IF THE SWEEP COMES BACK BELOW 0.61 ON THE NAMED PAIR, STOP AND INVESTIGATE THE HARNESS BEFORE THE DESIGN: (a) tools/check_dna_declarations.py, because a value the code cannot reach falls back to the default and prints identical tiles; (b) <out>/_rejects.json, because both exports are String enums and Object.set() on a typed property of the wrong type is refused in SILENCE - which is how tier_terrarium published ten tiles of its own default; (c) whether the sheet was captured with --max=12, because the cross product is 4 x 3 = 12 against build_dna_gallery's default cap of 9, and the trim comes off the tail of the LATER axis - which would delete the entire `web` column, meaning the whole context this prediction names.

designed_nulls.why: IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THE NULL IS THE FINDING RATHER THAN A CHECK ON IT. _ratio_gap returns immediately at r >= 0.5 and _fill_gap returns immediately at fill >= 1.0, so at fused (0.60 / 1.35) and at contact (0.50 / 1.00) both benches draw nothing at all and both frames are the four court meshes and no more. The replica measures 0.000 percent. WHAT MAKES IT THE FINDING: the two mechanisms have different arithmetic for the clear span - 2R(1 - 2r) on the ratio bench, (1 - fill)*LEAF on the fill bench - and those two expressions cross zero at the SAME RUNG OF THE SAME WORD, and are negative at the same one above it. Everywhere else on this sheet the two members disagree about what packing means; here they agree exactly, and the agreement is a pair of empty courts. Anything above 0.3 percent is render noise. Anything above 2 percent means a gate is not firing and a gap is being drawn with a negative or zero span, which would make every gap-row number in the sheet a fact about a sign error.

dna.designed_nulls_why: ONE FULL-FRAME NULL, AND TWO HALF-FRAME IDENTITIES THAT ARE REAL BUT NOT REGISTRABLE - recorded rather than quietly dropped, because both say the same thing the exhibit says. (1) UNDER `web`, THE ENTIRE RIGHT BENCH IS IDENTICAL AT open AND dust: 125 dots on a packing-independent lattice and zero rods in both. It is an exact identity across half the frame at two different values of the axis, and it is the sharpest statement this court can make - but a null must be a pair of FRAMES, and the left bench moves, so it is registered as the predicted_degeneracy instead where it can be measured against its own ranking. (2) UNDER `web`, THE RIGHT BENCH IS ALSO IDENTICAL AT fused AND contact, for a second and different reason: it draws the same 125 dots AND the same 406 incidences, because no leaf pair in the lattice sits at a Chebyshev distance between 1.00 and 1.35 pitches, so the contact graph cannot tell the two values apart. A lattice's incidence structure is quantised and a dilation below the next shell is invisible to it. THREE OTHER NULLS WERE CONSIDERED AND ARE NOT CONSTRUCTIBLE. A `cell` reading drawing the allotments alone would have been null across the whole packing axis on the fill bench and identical to `kept` on the ratio bench, which is two degeneracies rather than one and is refused under `declines`. Framing the two benches as separate variants of one bench would have made a null of the court furniture, which is furniture rather than an axis. And there is no null anywhere in `kept`: the ratio bench redraws 21 rings at four different radii in four different places, so every pair of that row is a new picture, which is what a generative parameter does and precisely what the other member's cannot.
dna.fixture_why: NOTHING TO PIN, and that is worth stating because one source needed it badly. example_8_3_recursion_circles_vr had to declare rotation_speed: 0.0 as a fixture, since its tori tumble at a rate that depends on depth - a sweep at a fixed settle time would have compared five ring counts at five tumble phases and handed the critic pose difference dressed as axis difference. This court has no time domain at all: no _process, no Timer, no tween, no AnimationPlayer. It also has no sampling to seed - no RandomNumberGenerator, no randf, no randi, no FastNoiseLite anywhere in the file - so a variant is a fact rather than a sample and no seed export exists to fixture. Every vertex is arithmetic on the eleven constants at the top of the script and the two tables transcribed from the sources.
dna.framing_why: 0.56, and the subject is wide and flat so the default would have wasted the frame. The union AABB is 2.4000 x 1.1519 x 1.1500 and the camera fits the DIAGONAL, 2.899882, so at framing 1.0 the frame would be 5.510 m across for a court whose projected width is 2.514 m - 46 percent of the frame width and about 21 percent of its area, with the marks that carry the axes at 6 to 12 px. At 0.56 the frame is 3.085475 m and the court fills 81 percent of the width; the replica reads the subject at 8.8 to 18.9 percent of frame across the twelve cells, which is sparse-not-small and is the correct reading of a court that is mostly floor by design. It is not tightened further because the fill bench reaches x = 1.122 and z = +-0.522 at fused, and cropping the court's own edge would make the AABB a fact about which value was picked.
dna.kin: THE TWO SOURCES ARE THE WHOLE FAMILY - two members, one comparison, nothing to triangulate - and this court exists because that is exactly the shape in which a false friend survives longest. THE NEXT RING OUT IS THE `tick` LADDER, and it is the reason both members had a second axis to spare: cantor_set, zeno_staircase, sierpinski_pyramid, menger_sponge and cube_subdivision share tick = once | coarse | fine | dense | limit, character for character, for a rule reapplied to a SET. example_8_3 refused that word on the record and gave its reason - its branch is 4-fold, so `limit` would be 5,461 tori, `a word whose top value cannot be drawn is a word taken without its answers` (gd:38-39) - and took `depth` from the L-system family instead. Both refusals are correct and they are refusals about the SAME lesson, which is how the two halves ended up sharing only the second word. THE WORD SIERPINSKI DECLINED IS `removal`, cantor_set's, and its reason is worth keeping because it is nearly this court's `gap` reading: Cantor's removed middles are a clean disjoint complement that can be ghosted back in, and a recursion whose children interpenetrate has no complement to draw (gd:38-43). That reasoning is sound for the source's own six-child build, where the top child's half-extent is 2.25 against a lattice offset of 2.00 - and it stops being true once the build is repaired, which is why this court can draw a gap at all. removal_room holds the other end of that thread. fractal_recursion_circles is a SECOND registry name on example_8_3's scene and is deliberately undeclared upstream; it is not a third member and must not be counted as one.
declines: THE BRIEF'S HYPOTHESIS THAT THE TWO MEMBERS ARE BUILT BY OPPOSITE OPERATIONS - circles ADD children into the space a parent leaves, Sierpinski REMOVES a sub-simplex at every step. IT IS FALSE IN THE CODE, and the source says so itself. _recursive_build (SierpinskiPyramid.gd:99-180) is purely additive: six positive recursive calls and not one subtraction, complement, skip or mask anywhere in the file. Sierpinski-by-removal is a way of TALKING about the set; this member builds it as an iterated function system of contractive maps, which is structurally the same kind of construction as the circles' four. The file's own DNA header at gd:38-43 already argues this when it refuses cantor_set's word `removal` on the grounds that its declined positions are not a clean complement. Both members are additive IFS. The real opposition is elsewhere and is the exhibit: one consumes packing INSIDE the recursion and one AFTER it.

THE BRIEF'S ARITHMETIC AND ITS CONCLUSION THAT `dust` IS UNREACHABLE FOR THE PYRAMID BY CONSTRUCTION. Three corrections, in order. The classic Sierpinski tetrahedron keeps 4 children at half scale, log(4)/log(2) = 2 exactly, and the brief is right about that one. This artifact is not that: its @identity says five children (log(5)/log(2) = 2.3219) and its CODE makes six (log(6)/log(2) = 2.5850), so the dimension the brief computed belongs to a third object. And the conclusion does not follow either way, because `packing` is not a dimension knob in this member at all: PACKING_FILL is read only in _spawn_cube, after every leaf position is fixed, so the dimension is constant across all four values and `dust` is perfectly reachable - it removes 97.8 percent of the drawn volume at unchanged extent, census and dimension. THE BRIEF'S ERROR IS THE INSTRUCTIVE PART: it assumed packing was the same KIND of parameter in both members, which is the hypothesis the wave was set to test, and it is the assumption the court disproves.

REPRODUCING THE SOURCE'S SIX-CHILD BUILD AND ITS OFF-BY-TWO LATTICE. Both were tempting - a synthesis that photographs what the corpus actually places is worth something - and both were refused for one reason: a court whose `contact` column is a four-to-one overlap is a photograph of a bug, not of a word, and the whole point of this bench is to ask what the word means. The faults are reported here and in the script header with their line numbers instead, which is where a finding belongs. Note what this costs and it is real: the right bench here is NOT what any of the six live sierpinski_pyramid placements looks like. It is what that file's own @identity and its own gd:198 comment say it should look like.

A THIRD AXIS FOR THE RECURSION COUNT - sierpinski's `tick` or example_8_3's `depth`. Refused twice over. It belongs to the sources and both already carry it, so sweeping it here would sweep one question under two names; and it would make the sheet 4 x 3 x 5 = 60 cells, where the trim off the tail of the last axis at any sane --max deletes the axis the experiment is about. The depths are fixed at 3 on both benches (21 rings and 125 leaves), chosen so the two censuses are within 20 percent of each other and neither bench outweighs the other in the critic's luminance measure.

A `cell` READING - the allotments alone, each atom's denominator drawn as a cage. It was the strongest-sounding third value and it is refused on two counts. It is the union of `kept` and `gap` by volume, and a value that is secretly the union of its own axis is exactly what wave 20 found six times and ruled out. And it is half-degenerate on top of that: the ratio mechanism has NO denominator distinct from its numerator - the child's allotment is bounded by its own tangency to the parent, so cell and atom coincide - which would have made the left half of that row a repeat of `kept` at every value, while the right half was null across the whole packing axis. That the value cannot be built is itself the finding restated: only one of these two mechanisms has a cell for the atom to claim a fraction of.

AN `all` OR `both` VALUE ON EITHER AXIS, and a `shadow` reading that projects the atoms onto the floor. The first for wave 20's reason. The second because a floor projection at pitch -0.26 is foreshortened to about a quarter of its true area and would have been measured as a faint axis rather than a real one - the projection is the right idea for a dimension argument and the wrong idea for this standpoint, and probe_anamorphic is the honest way to ask for it later rather than shipping a value that only works from above.

THE SOURCES' COLOUR AND THE SOURCES' LINE WEIGHTS. example_8_3 dresses every torus in mat_pop_plastic, a shader material, and a stale compiled shader reads as INERT in this pipeline; sierpinski instantiates cube_scene.tscn, which carries a StaticBody3D and a CollisionShape3D per leaf - 1296 of them at the shipped depth. Both are replaced by plain StandardMaterial3D and plain BoxMesh here, and the two benches are matched in luminance and separated only in hue, so neither half can set every number in the sheet on weight alone. The ring gauge is held constant at 16 mm at all three generations, which is a departure from the source's proportional tube (inner = 0.9 x radius): at r = 0.25 a proportional tube on the third generation is 1.25 mm and invisible. The gauge is the PEN and holding it fixed is what stops packing from moving the ink weight as well as the geometry.

ANIMATION, AND EVERY RATE IN BOTH SOURCES. example_8_3 carries rotation_speed, rotation_per_depth and pause_duration - three of its five original exports are rates, invisible to a still - and it runs _process every frame, which is why it had to declare rotation_speed: 0.0 as a fixture. sierpinski_pyramid is @tool and rebuilds live in the editor. This court has neither, and the absence is load-bearing rather than stylistic: it is the reason two builds of one cell are the same mesh and the reason a diff between two cells means anything.
dna.sweep_note: --max=12 IS MANDATORY AND THE COST OF THE DEFAULT IS THE EXPERIMENT. The cross product is 4 x 3 = 12 against build_dna_gallery's cap of 9, and the trim comes off the tail of the LATER axis, which is `reading`. At the default the sheet renders as 4 x 2 - kept and gap only - which deletes the entire `web` column: the context the predicted_degeneracy names, the reading in which the fill bench's lattice is shown not to move, and the only place the two half-frame identities in designed_nulls_why can be seen. What survives is a finished-looking eight-tile sheet in which both axes bite and the finding is absent.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry from the file's own constants; no Godot was run. x is the floor slab, 2.400. y runs from the slab's underside at -0.050 to the fill bench's highest corner at fused, 1.1019, which is C_FILL.y 0.58 plus half the leaf-centre extent 0.875/2 plus half a fused leaf 0.125 x 1.35 / 2. z is the slab, 1.150, against a fill bench reaching +-0.522 at the same value. The union is taken across all twelve cells, which is what capture_config_sweep frames against.
